Class OnixSettingReorderableEnum

Namespace
OnixRuntime.Api.OnixClient.Settings
Assembly
OnixRuntime.dll

Represents An enum that you can optionally allow enabling/disabling the values of. The user gets entries they can move around at the minimum. It supports having values with the same name be treated differently. This is a complex setting type, you definitely want to use the helper functions rather than interact with the data too directly unless you're making UI. You can use ReorderableEnumValue for your config class.

public class OnixSettingReorderableEnum : OnixSetting, IDisposable, IEnumerable<OnixSettingReorderableEnum.Entry>, IEnumerable

Constructors

OnixSettingReorderableEnum(OnixModule?, string, string, List<Entry>, bool, SettingChangedDelegate?)

Creates a reorderable enum setting from the list of entries.

public OnixSettingReorderableEnum(OnixModule? mod, string name, string description, List<OnixSettingReorderableEnum.Entry> entries, bool allowDisablingEntries, OnixSetting.SettingChangedDelegate? changeCallback = null)

Parameters

mod OnixModule

The module to add this setting to, can be null to insert it into the mod yourself later.

name string

The name of the setting, that displays as a title. If you don't want that, you can pass "" to disable it.

description string

The description of the setting, will show as a tooltip.

entries List<OnixSettingReorderableEnum.Entry>

The entries the user can order around.

allowDisablingEntries bool

If true, the user will be given a toggle for all entries. Those entries should then be skipped or treated as disabled.

changeCallback OnixSetting.SettingChangedDelegate

A callback to be called whenever this setting changes.

Remarks

You must never look at that entries list again, I'm taking that fully and breaking it.

SetEntries(IEnumerable<Entry>, bool)

Sets the new list of entries. You should never use any of those entries again, don't use the list it came from. You should use the helper functions whenever possible instead of dealing with raw entries like that.
